{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
A '''sequence number''' is a consecutive number in a [[sequence]] of numbers, usually of [[Real number|real]] [[Integer|integers]] ([[Natural number|natural numbers]]). Sequence numbers have many practical applications. They can be used, among other things, as part of [[Serial number|serial numbers]] on manufactured parts, in case management,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ordbøkene.no - Bokmålsordboka og Nynorskordboka |url=https://ordbokene.no/bm,nn/ordbokene.no |access-date=2024-02-26 |language=no}}</ref> or in [[Database|databases]] as a [[surrogate key]] for registering and identifying unique entries in a [[Table (database)|table]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sequences | website=[[IBM]] |url=https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/db2/11.5?topic=objects-sequences |access-date=2024-02-26 |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=MashaMSFT |date=2023-04-18 |title=Sequence Numbers - SQL Server |url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/sequence-numbers/sequence-numbers?view=sql-server-ver16 |access-date=2024-02-26 |language=en-us}}</ref> (in which case it is used as a [[primary key]]).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roeser |first=Mary Beth |title=CREATE SEQUENCE |url=https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/CREATE-SEQUENCE.html#GUID-E9C78A8C-615A-4757-B2A8-5E6EFB130571 |access-date=2024-02-26 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=SQL Server: Sequences (Autonumber) |url=https://www.techonthenet.com/sql_server/sequences.php |access-date=2024-02-26}}</ref>

== Examples ==
Historically, the [[Norwegian Mapping Authority]] have used sequence numbers for [[land registration]] as a [[Placeholder name|placeholder]] in cases where an organization number or [[National identity number (Norway)|national identity number]] have not been known.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-27 |title=Navneendring, fisjon og fusjon |url=https://kartverket.no/eiendom/overfore-eiendom/navneendring-fisjon-og-fusjon |access-date=2024-02-26 |language=nb-NO}}</ref>

In [[elections in Norway]], sequence numbers are used in the duplicate check to prevent votes being counted twice or to detect duplicate [[Ballot|ballots]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Endelig opptelling - Valgmedarbeiderportalen |url=https://valgmedarbeiderportalen.valg.no/eva/opptelling/endelig-opptelling/ |access-date=2024-02-26}}</ref>

An example of a sequence number being used as a surrogate key is the ''snr'' number used by [[Statistics Norway]] since 1970,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Vangen |first=Torill |title=Snr |url=https://www.ssb.no/a/metadata/conceptvariable/vardok/500043/nb |access-date=2024-02-26 |language=nb}}</ref> which uniquely identifies a person even if their social security number changes. The snr number will then be linked to both social security numbers, and act as a link that ensures that each person can be identified by a unique key at all times.<ref name=":0" />

== Comparison with serial number ==
A distinction is sometimes made between a sequence number and a serial number. For example, a Swiss [[locomotive]] may have the designation "[[RegioExpress|Re]] 465 003-2",<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sveitsiske lok- og motorvognbetegnelser, er de kryptiske ? Del 2 – M&E |url=https://www.modellelektro.no/test/1998/02/15/hei-sveits-sveitsiske-lok-og-motorvognbetegnelser-er-de-kryptiske-del-2/ |access-date=2024-02-26 |language=nb-NO}}</ref> where:

* 465 is the serial number, and stands for 4 [[Drive shaft|drive shafts]], 6th version, and 5 for the company [[BLS AG|BLS]]
* 003 is the sequence number, and means that it is the third locomotive in this series
* -2 is a [[check digit]]
